transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, um… thanks for seeing me. I guess the main reason I came in is work-related. I process insurance claims, and I’ve been having this problem where I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish my claim reviews. It’s not like I’m trying to avoid work, exactly… I just keep finding myself up and away from my desk, and it’s starting to feel like something I should get help with, if that makes sense.
Do you feel anxious or worried when you're sitting at your desk working on claims?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I wouldn’t describe it as anxiety exactly. I’m not sitting there feeling panicky or worried about the claims, at least not that I’ve noticed. It’s more like… I just end up not staying put. But I don’t know if I’m explaining that the right way.
Do you have any recurring thoughts that you can't stop thinking about?

Um… recurring thoughts? I don’t think so. Not in the sense of something looping in my head that I can’t stop thinking about. I mean, I can get stuck on normal work stuff sometimes, but I wouldn’t say there’s one thought that keeps coming back or that feels out of my control. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel like you have to get up from your desk for some reason, like something is compelling you to do so?

I don’t know if I’d say it feels like I’m compelled exactly… that sounds a little stronger than how it feels to me. But yeah, the main thing is I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish my claim reviews. It’s like I just don’t stay put the way I should.
Do you feel restless in your body when you're sitting at your desk?

Yeah… maybe a little. I don’t know if I’d call it “restless” exactly, but in longer meetings or trainings I do notice I’m kind of bouncing my leg or clicking a pen, shifting around in the chair. I’m usually trying to still look focused, so I don’t think it’s super obvious, but… yeah, I guess my body doesn’t totally stay still.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

I don’t think so, not in a big way. I mean, I probably do small things without fully thinking them through sometimes, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’m especially impulsive or doing risky stuff without considering it. At least, nothing really comes to mind. Does that seem like what you’re asking?
Do you find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're not at work, like when you're at home or out with friends?

A little, yeah… I mean, I notice it more in settings where I’m supposed to be sitting still, like trainings or longer team meetings. I’ll be bouncing my leg or clicking a pen or shifting around in the chair, even when I’m trying to look focused. I don’t know if it’s that noticeable to other people, but I do catch myself doing it.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?

Hmm… I’m not sure. I don’t think I have, like, the same thought repeating over and over in a way I can’t stop. My mind can wander, but I wouldn’t describe it as repetitive thoughts exactly. Is that what you mean, or are you asking more like worrying about something?
Do you feel restless when you're relaxing or doing leisure activities, like watching TV or reading a book?

A little, I guess. It’s more obvious in situations where I’m supposed to sit still, like trainings or longer team meetings. I’ll catch myself bouncing my leg, clicking my pen, or shifting around in the chair, even if I’m trying to look focused. I don’t know if it’s a big deal, but it does happen.
Do you have difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work?

I’m not totally sure… I mean, I try to be careful at work, especially with details. I don’t know if I’d say it’s a big problem. Maybe once in a while I might miss something small, but I usually try to double-check so it doesn’t turn into an issue. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel restless when you're doing quiet activities by yourself, like reading or listening to music?

Yeah, a bit. I think it shows up more when I’m supposed to sit still somewhere, like in trainings or longer team meetings. I’ll be bouncing my leg or clicking my pen, or just shifting around in the chair, even when I’m trying to look like I’m paying attention. I’m not sure if that counts for quiet activities by myself too, but it’s kind of that same restless feeling, I guess.
Do you find it hard to focus on one thing for a long time?

Yeah, I think so… not all the time, but at work especially. If I’m reading through a claim and people nearby start talking about another case, or I suddenly remember some random errand I need to do, my attention kind of slides off. Then I realize I didn’t actually take in what I just read, so I have to reread the same section a few times. I try to catch it, but yeah, it does happen.
Do you experience these feelings of restlessness and difficulty staying focused at night, or is it mainly during the day?

I’m not totally sure I’ve noticed a pattern at night, honestly. I think I notice it more during the day, like when I’m working or in meetings. At night I’m usually not tracking it as much… I might just be tired or trying to unwind, so it’s harder for me to say. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you experience restlessness when you're alone at home?

I’m not really sure, honestly. When I’m home alone I don’t pay as much attention to it, because I can kind of move around if I need to and nobody’s watching. I wouldn’t say it’s a major thing I’ve noticed… maybe just normal fidgeting sometimes? I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Do you experience restlessness in multiple situations throughout your day, not just at work?

Yeah… I think it’s not only at work. Like in trainings or longer team meetings, I’ll catch myself bouncing my leg or clicking my pen, or just shifting around in the chair a lot. I’m trying to look like I’m paying attention, so I don’t think it’s super obvious, but it does happen in those kinds of situations too. Does that count as restlessness?
Do you feel restless when you're in a quiet, comfortable environment, like your own home?

At home when it’s quiet… I don’t know, I’m not sure I’d call it restless exactly. I might shift around or get up if I feel like it, but since I’m comfortable and nobody’s expecting me to sit still, I don’t notice it as much. So I guess I haven’t really paid attention to it in that setting. Does that make sense?
Do you think your restlessness is usually triggered by feeling anxious or overwhelmed?

I don’t think it’s always anxiety, no. I mean, sometimes if I’m stressed it probably makes it worse, but in trainings or longer team meetings I’ll notice I’m bouncing my leg or clicking my pen, or shifting around in the chair even when I’m trying to look focused. It’s not like I’m panicking or anything… it just kind of happens. Does that answer what you mean?
Has your restlessness affected your personal relationships or daily activities outside of work?

Um… outside of work, I’m not really sure. I don’t think it’s caused any big issues, at least not that I’ve noticed. Like, I might move around or fidget a bit, but I don’t think anyone close to me has really complained about it or anything.

For daily stuff, I guess I haven’t paid as much attention to whether it affects things. It feels more noticeable when I’m expected to sit still somewhere. Does that answer it okay?
Has your restlessness been a problem for you for more than 6 months?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but the stuff at work has been going on since the department got reorganized, which was about… 15 months ago now. That’s when I started noticing it more, at least in those work situations. Does that count as more than 6 months?
Have you experienced these symptoms of restlessness and difficulty staying focused for most days over the past 6 months?

Yeah, I think so… at least with the work stuff. It’s not like every single minute of every day, but the restlessness and trouble staying focused have been showing up pretty regularly since the department reorganization, which was about 15 months ago. So… yes, over the past 6 months for sure, I’d say. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
